title: Which Holds More?
subject: math
learningGoal: Compare capacity by filling and counting equal cups, not by how a container looks.
realWorldHook: Cooks and gardeners need to know how much a container holds, and tall isn't always more.

materials.householdSubstitution: Any two cups, bowls or clean jars
Dry rice or sand for a no-spill version

noPurchaseRoute: Use any two kitchen containers and a scoop; dry rice works if you want to avoid water.
parentPreview: Your child predicts which container holds more, then tests by counting scoops of water. Tall containers often fool us.

parent.parentSays: Which of these holds more? Just look, don't touch.
parent.whyThisWorks: A prediction based on looks sets up a useful surprise.

child.readAloudText: Which one holds more? Just look.

parent.parentSays: Fill the tall one scoop by scoop. Count the scoops. Keep each scoop level.
parent.whyThisWorks: Equal scoops make a fair unit, like the hand spans or cubes.

child.screen: Fill the tall one. Count the scoops.
child.readAloudText: Fill the tall one. Count the scoops.

parent.parentSays: Now the wide one. Count again.

child.screen: Now the wide one. Count the scoops.
child.readAloudText: Now the wide one. Count the scoops.

parent.parentSays: Which held more scoops? Was your guess right?
Ask the two check questions below. Give your child time to think, then note how each one went.
Were you surprised? Why can tall containers trick our eyes?

child.readAloudText: You tested how much things hold.

misconceptions.signal: Insists the taller one holds more even after counting.
misconceptions.supportiveNextQuestion: The numbers say something different from our eyes. Which should we trust?
If some scoops are only half full, is our count fair?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: Cup A holds 6 scoops, cup B holds 9 scoops. Which holds more?

interpretation.clear: Says B and how many more.
interpretation.not_yet: Picks by looks or says A.

child.screen: Cup A: 6 scoops. Cup B: 9 scoops. Which holds more?
child.readAloudText: Cup A holds six scoops. Cup B holds nine. Which holds more?

checkQuestions.parentAsks: How could we find out which bath toy bucket holds more?

interpretation.clear: Suggests filling with the same scoop and counting.

child.screen: How could you find which bucket holds more?
child.readAloudText: How could you find which bucket holds more? Tell your grown-up.

extension: Pour from one container into the other. What happens? Does it overflow?

shorterVersion.description: Use dry rice and compare two cups by pouring one into the other.

accessibilityAdaptations: Use dry rice to avoid spills.
Use a bigger scoop so there are fewer to count.
